title: introduce-credential-fanout-and-typed-stream-hooks-unify-retry-profiles-and-ts-sdk-bump
author: Nina Patel
body: Motivation: Multiple SDKs (TS/Python/Go) had divergent approaches to streaming token refresh and retry presets which led to subtly different developer ergonomics and intermittent reconnect bugs in long-running multi-connection workloads. This change introduces a lightweight 'credential fanout' abstraction that allows a single lease/refresh pipeline to fan out credentials to multiple stream connections, plus typed stream lifecycle hooks so SDK consumers can run warmup/cleanup logic deterministically. Scope: 1) core credential/fanout implementation (shared, low-dep runtime) 2) TypeScript SDK surface changes (typed hooks, new RetryProfiles enum, default backoff presets) and minor ergonomic helpers 3) Python/Go companion shims in the monorepo that wire the new contract into existing session managers (non-breaking) 4) test harness updates, docs, and changelog bumps. Key goals: 1) reduce duplicate refresh requests under high fan-out, 2) provide deterministic hook points for warmup/backpressure in streaming consumers, 3) unify retry/backoff presets across SDKS, 4) bump TS SDK to 1.7.0 with clear migration notes. Checklist: - [x] implement credential fanout and fanout-safe refresh semantics - [x] add typed stream hooks (onOpen, onWarmup, onClose) for TS SDK - [x] expose RetryProfiles enum and default presets - [x] add shim adapters for Python and Go SDKs (no behavior change by default) - [x] update e2e streaming treadmill tests and flaky test stabilization - [x] update changelogs and release notes - [x] manual smoke tests with Canary app (stream fanout=12) Changes: commits below and high level file list show exact edits. Testing: Unit tests cover fanout edgecases (concurrent refresh, lease expiry, single-refresh-per-window). Integration tests on CI include streaming treadmill at fanout sizes 1/4/12 and an emulated token expiry. One flaky test (stream-resume-interop) failed on first CI run, was stabilized by a 150ms delay in the test harness to avoid race with test-only hook; CI was re-run and all checks passed. Migration notes: TS SDK consumers who relied on internal session internals should switch to the exported typed hooks; default behavior is unchanged and migration helper is provided in the deprecation guide. Rollout: merged to main and will be included in the 1.7.0 SDK release cut later this week. See release_notes field below for user-facing notes.

review_comments: Marco Ruiz: Please ensure we don't forget metrics on the fanout path (fanout.size, fanout.refresh_count). Add counters and labels so we can alert if refresh amplification appears.

Leah Tan: The typed hooks look good; can we make onWarmup async and document expected latency impact?
Nina Patel (author): onWarmup is async in the exported typings; added note in docs about typical latency expectations and suggested usage patterns.
Danielle O'Connor: CI treadmill flaky test fix makes sense but add a TODO to remove the artificial delay once the event ordering is hardened.

merge_result: Merged by squash on 2025-08-18 after approvals from Marco Ruiz and Leah Tan. Merge method: squash. Release action queued to cut TS SDK 1.7.0. Changelog entry added to packages/ts-sdk/CHANGELOG.md.
release_notes: TS SDK 1.7.0: Introduces credential-fanout abstraction to reduce refresh amplification under high fanout streaming workloads; new typed stream hooks (onOpen/onWarmup/onClose) for deterministic warmup and cleanup; unified RetryProfiles enum with sensible defaults that align with other SDKs; Python/Go shims included for compatibility. Migration: default behavior is unchanged. If you used internal session objects, follow the migration guide at docs/sdk/migration/typed-hooks.md to adopt exported hooks.
